title: Domain V: Leadership & Influence - Leadership & Influence - Partnerships & Outreach
subject: Leadership & Influence

questions.q: What is the primary objective of a procurement department hosting a 'Reverse Trade Show'?
options: To allow vendors to display their products and sell directly to agency executives.
For agency procurement staff and end-users to host booths, allowing vendors to circulate and learn how to do business with the agency.
To auction off surplus agency equipment to the general public.
To force vendors to bid against each other in real-time.
questions.explain: In a reverse trade show, the typical roles are reversed: the buyers/agencies sit at the booths, and the vendors walk the floor to meet them, learn about upcoming opportunities, and understand the agency's procurement processes.
questions.subject: Leadership & Influence

questions.q: When forming an evaluation committee for a complex software implementation, which approach best utilizes cross-functional partnerships?
options: Selecting only procurement staff to ensure strict adherence to rules.
Selecting representatives from IT, finance, end-users, and project management to ensure all perspectives are evaluated.
Allowing the vendor to select the committee members they prefer.
Choosing only executive-level management to speed up the process.
questions.explain: Cross-functional teams bring diverse expertise. Including IT (technical), finance (budget), end-users (functionality), and PM (execution) ensures a comprehensive evaluation and builds agency-wide consensus and buy-in for the final award.
questions.subject: Leadership & Influence

questions.q: An agency has set a strategic goal to increase participation from Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprises (MWBE). Which outreach strategy is most effective?
options: Wait for MWBE vendors to find the agency's website and register.
Partner with local chambers of commerce and advocacy groups to host targeted 'How to do Business with Us' workshops.
Automatically award contracts to MWBE firms regardless of price.
Waive all insurance requirements for MWBE vendors.
questions.explain: Active partnership and outreach involve going into the community. Collaborating with advocacy groups and hosting targeted educational workshops demystifies the procurement process and actively encourages diverse vendor participation without violating competitive principles.
questions.subject: Leadership & Influence

questions.q: To build a stronger partnership with an operational department that frequently submits emergency requisitions, the procurement professional should:
options: Deny all future emergency requests.
Implement a quarterly forecasting meeting with the department to identify upcoming needs before they become emergencies.
Report the department head to internal audit.
Delegate procurement authority entirely to the department.
questions.explain: Partnership involves solving root problems collaboratively. Regular forecasting meetings build relationships, improve planning, and reduce the frequency of preventable emergencies through proactive procurement.
questions.subject: Leadership & Influence

questions.q: What is the strategic value of conducting a vendor debriefing with an unsuccessful offeror?
options: To provide the vendor with the winning vendor's trade secrets.
To give the losing vendor a chance to negotiate a sub-contract.
To help the vendor understand weaknesses in their proposal, encouraging them to submit more competitive proposals in the future.
To justify lowering the vendor's past performance rating.
questions.explain: Vendor debriefings are an outreach tool. By constructively discussing areas for improvement, the agency helps develop the vendor community, leading to better, more competitive proposals in future solicitations.
questions.subject: Leadership & Influence

questions.q: Which of the following describes 'Supplier Relationship Management' (SRM) as a partnership tool?
options: Using aggressive tactics to force the lowest possible price out of a vendor.
A comprehensive approach to managing an agency's interactions with organizations that supply goods and services, fostering collaboration to maximize value.
Exclusively communicating with vendors through legal counsel.
Rotating vendors annually to ensure no relationships are formed.
questions.explain: SRM is a strategic approach that seeks to foster collaborative partnerships with key suppliers. Instead of an adversarial approach, SRM focuses on mutual value creation, innovation, and risk reduction.
questions.subject: Leadership & Influence

questions.q: During an RFP evaluation, an external stakeholder serving on the committee fails to read the proposals and scores randomly. How should the procurement official handle this to protect the partnership and process?
options: Accept the scores to avoid upsetting the stakeholder.
Privately discuss the importance of objective evaluation with the stakeholder, offering guidance on how to score based on criteria; remove their scores if they refuse to comply.
Berate the stakeholder in front of the committee.
Cancel the RFP entirely.
questions.explain: The procurement official must protect the integrity of the process while managing the relationship. A private, corrective conversation emphasizes the legal importance of objective scoring. If compliance fails, the scores must be excluded to prevent a flawed award.
questions.subject: Leadership & Influence

questions.q: An agency is forming an Interlocal Agreement (cooperative partnership) with a neighboring county to purchase winter road salt. What is the primary mutual benefit?
options: Bypassing the need for public transparency.
Combining volume to achieve economies of scale and reducing administrative duplication.
Avoiding local vendor preference laws.
Shifting liability entirely to the neighboring county.
questions.explain: Cooperative partnerships (Interlocal agreements) aggregate the demand (volume) of multiple agencies to achieve better pricing (economies of scale) while sharing the administrative effort of the bidding process.
questions.subject: Leadership & Influence

questions.q: To increase market competition for an upcoming, highly specialized infrastructure project, the procurement department hosts an 'Industry Day.' The main purpose of this event is to:
options: Select the winning vendor before the bid is officially published.
Share project visions with the market, gather industry feedback on feasibility, and allow prime contractors to network with sub-contractors.
Solicit campaign donations for local politicians.
Collect vendor registration fees to fund the procurement department.
questions.explain: Industry Days are proactive outreach tools used for complex projects. They inform the market, gather valuable feedback to refine the SOW, and facilitate networking between prime and sub-contractors, enhancing overall competition.
questions.subject: Leadership & Influence

questions.q: A newly established centralized procurement department is facing resistance from a department that previously handled its own purchasing. To build a successful partnership, the Chief Procurement Officer should initially focus on:
options: Auditing all of the department's past purchases to find errors.
Listening to the department's unique operational needs and demonstrating how centralization will improve their efficiency.
Revoking all p-cards immediately.
Refusing to process their requisitions until they apologize.
questions.explain: Overcoming resistance requires change management and relationship building. Listening actively and addressing 'What's in it for them?' (e.g., efficiency, reduced liability) fosters collaboration rather than defensiveness.
questions.subject: Leadership & Influence

questions.q: When establishing a partnership with a critical vendor, the procurement professional must balance collaboration with:
options: Total secrecy from the public.
Maintaining appropriate professional boundaries and independence.
Ensuring the vendor loses money on the contract.
Ignoring contract terms to keep the vendor happy.
questions.explain: While collaborative vendor relationships (SRM) are valuable, public procurement professionals must never compromise their independence or ethics. They must maintain professional boundaries to avoid conflicts of interest or the appearance of favoritism.
questions.subject: Leadership & Influence

questions.q: To streamline outreach to new businesses, an agency publishes a 'Vendor Manual' on its website. This document should primarily contain:
options: Detailed financial records of the agency.
Step-by-step instructions on how to register, where to find solicitations, invoice procedures, and ethics policies.
The direct cell phone numbers of all agency directors.
A list of prices paid to existing vendors.
questions.explain: A Vendor Manual serves as an educational and outreach tool, helping new suppliers navigate the bureaucracy of public procurement by outlining registration, bidding rules, invoicing, and ethical expectations.
questions.subject: Leadership & Influence

questions.q: A procurement department teams up with the agency's Legal and Risk Management departments to create a standardized set of contract terms and conditions. What is the primary benefit of this internal partnership?
options: It shifts all procurement liability to the risk management department.
It ensures consistency, reduces negotiation cycle times, and effectively mitigates organizational risk.
It eliminates the need for procurement to read contracts.
It allows vendors to dictate the terms.
questions.explain: Partnering with legal and risk to create standardized terms establishes a cohesive agency defense, ensures legal compliance, speeds up the contracting process, and reduces the time spent negotiating individual clauses.
questions.subject: Leadership & Influence

questions.q: You are leading a cross-functional team tasked with sourcing a new ERP software system. The IT department and the Finance department fiercely disagree on the system's required functionality. As the procurement lead, your role is to:
options: Side with the department that has the larger budget.
Facilitate a consensus-building workshop focused on identifying shared agency goals and drafting objective specifications that meet both needs.
Cancel the project until they resolve the dispute.
Make the technical decision yourself to save time.
questions.explain: Procurement often serves as a neutral facilitator in internal partnerships. Guiding disparate departments toward consensus by focusing on shared strategic goals and best value ensures the resulting specifications are functional and competitive.
questions.subject: Leadership & Influence

questions.q: A local vendor feels they have been treated unfairly because they haven't won a contract in two years. They escalate their complaint to the agency director. As part of vendor outreach, what is the best approach for the procurement professional?
options: Ban the vendor from future bidding for complaining.
Offer the vendor a small contract directly to appease them.
Schedule a meeting with the vendor to transparently review their past bid submissions, explain evaluation criteria, and discuss how to improve future responses.
Defend the procurement department's actions aggressively to the director and refuse to meet the vendor.
questions.explain: Effective outreach handles conflict through transparency and education. By reviewing past bids and explaining evaluation metrics, the procurement professional defuses tension, maintains impartiality, and helps the vendor become more competitive.
